proposed_facts.reason: Canonical declarations and assignments establish a b0 latch, signed sequence, coalescing pending flag, initialization resets, and advancement before unchecked output. The fixed buffer and signed arithmetic justify rejecting unlimited monotonicity.
The exact void signature and both idle and normal paths reaching the function end distinguish no returned value from non-returning behavior.

Independently verified the fewer-than-two-XFB flush bypass, waiting statuses, selection precedence, and non-returning assertion expansion. Assertion occurs before advancement and clearing; normal output status is ignored.
The dispatcher is debug-level-gated, conditionally refreshes two or four slots, and always checks four. Getters return stored masks; the owned checker delegates qualifying input to the shared toggle.

The checker does not mutate input masks. The producer's edge calculation and differing refresh/consumer bounds support possible repeated observations of stale pressed bits and multiple slot-driven toggles.

The owned canonical file confirms both input paths, old-sequence formatting after global advancement, selected-buffer output size, exact USB prefix stripping, and clearing pending after unchecked output.

Setup changes only the latch; the exported toggle invokes setter or reset. The reset implementation uses configured game_speed. Request persistence, initialization resets, filename reuse, and attempt-based sequence advancement follow from local control flow.
